headlines.text: On a Sunday in 2026, back when a new champion was crowned for the AEW International Title as Konosuke Takeshita vs. Kazuchika Okada battled it out, appearing on Double or Nothing, rated 9.52 ? an instant classic ? ending the champion's reign at 6 defenses. After months of a slow-building grudge, Takeshita finally toppled Okada for the AEW International Title ? only for a returning Kyle Fletcher to blindside his former Don Callis Family stablemate moments later.

It was 2023 when The Lucha Brothers vs. Castagnoli & Yuta fought tooth and nail for the ROH World Tag Team Titles, appearing on Dynamite, rated 7.26 ? a well-worked match. For Castagnoli & Yuta, it marked a first real shot at championship gold. Championship gold always raises the stakes.
Flash back to 2024, when Alex Windsor made a statement, debuting in the main event against Kris Statlander vs. Willow Nightingale vs. Anna Jay, appearing on Rampage, rated 6.27.

secondaries.text: That Sunday in 2026, it was title-change night for the AEW World Heavyweight Title as MJF vs. Darby Allin battled it out, appearing on Double or Nothing, rated 8.99 ? a war that left everything in the ring ? ending the champion's reign at 8 defenses. MJF reclaimed the AEW World Championship from Darby Allin in a brutal Title vs. Hair match, with Kevin Knight blindsiding the fallen former champion the moment the bell rang.

That Sunday in 2026, it was title-change night for the AEW World Tag Team Titles as Cage & Copeland vs. FTR battled it out, appearing on Double or Nothing, rated 8.24 ? one of the better matches of the year ? ending the champion's reign at 8 defenses. Christian Cage and Adam Copeland survived an "I Quit" New York Street Fight soaked in barbed wire and burning tables, dethroning FTR to become AEW World Tag Team Champions and saving their partnership in the process.
